question: How does spending differ by customer age group?
paraphrases: Which age group buys the most?
interpretation: Age is aggregate-only. Group in SQL with computed bands (10-year bands via FLOOR(age/10)*10) at the requested grain; never retrieve exact ages and re-bin in prose. Report buyers and spend per buyer, because raw revenue mostly reflects group size.
grain: 10-year age band, last 12 complete months, aggregate only
sql:
SELECT FLOOR(u.age / 10) * 10 AS age_band_from,
  FLOOR(u.age / 10) * 10 + 9 AS age_band_to,
  COUNT(DISTINCT u.id) AS buyers,
  ROUND(SUM(oi.sale_price), 2) AS completed_revenue,
  ROUND(SUM(oi.sale_price) / COUNT(DISTINCT u.id), 2) AS spend_per_buyer
FROM `bigquery-public-data.thelook_ecommerce.order_items` AS oi
JOIN `bigquery-public-data.thelook_ecommerce.users` AS u ON oi.user_id = u.id
WHERE oi.status = 'Complete'
  AND DATE(oi.created_at) >= DATE_SUB(DATE_TRUNC(CURRENT_DATE(), MONTH), INTERVAL 12 MONTH)
  AND DATE(oi.created_at) < DATE_TRUNC(CURRENT_DATE(), MONTH)
GROUP BY age_band_from, age_band_to
ORDER BY age_band_from
analyst_report:
Over <period>, the <largest_band> band has the most buyers, while <highest_value_band> spends the most per buyer (<spend_per_buyer>).
Caveats: aggregate-only; small bands are suppressed by policy; bands are 10 years wide as queried.
Actions: align campaign targeting with high-value bands; do not infer causality from age alone.
